doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Hearing the score on the scoring stage and dictating changes
summary: He discovers whether music works at the scoring stage and dictates fixes to the orchestra when producers ask.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Did you in the early days of your writing actually go to see the movie? Go to the theater and see the movie that you just scored? Or had you had it by then?

Yeah. I’m trying to remember if I did. I’m sure I did I just don’t recall offhand, because of course when you look at a movie or score it from the cue sheets you kind of know it inside out so it’s always good to know whether your music works with the movie and of course you find that out on the scoring stage with an orchestra and a playback. And you
know occasionally a producer or director will go, “Listen this part is bothering me, can we fix it?” So I say, “Yes, give me ten minutes” and then I go in the orchestra and start dictating changes.
To whatever musicians need to either stop doing what they’re doing or do more.
